title: Description field is bound to <meta name="description">, not the textarea: descriptions are never shown, edits are silently dropped
failure_scenario: field('description') runs document.querySelector('[name="description"]'), which matches the <meta name="description"> tag in <head> (line 7) before the #toolDescription textarea. fillEditor/formValues therefore read and write an expando on the meta element. (1) Opening any saved tool shows an empty 'What does it do?' box. (2) A user types a description for a new tool, saves, gets 'Tool saved' - the tool is stored with description '' and MCP clients see no description, which is the main signal an LLM uses to pick a tool. (3) Editing the description of an existing tool does not mark the form dirty, Save reports success, but the old description is kept; navigating away does not prompt. (4) After loading a template, the textarea still shows text from the previous draft, while the template's hidden description is what is actually saved.
evidence: Verified in Chromium (s4_desc.cjs): querySelector('[name="description"]').tagName === 'META'. big_numbers (API description 'Prints large ints and floats') opened with textarea ''. After typing 'New description typed by user': saveState stayed 'Enabled for AI · saved', toast 'Tool saved. Ready to Run / Test.', API description unchanged, leaving the page raised no prompt. New tool desc_probe typed 'Fetch the weather for a city' -> API description ''. Template node_basic: textarea still showed 'Fetch the weather for a city', meta expando held 'Return a greeting and UTC time...'; user cleared the textarea, saved -> API description 'Return a greeting and UTC time. No packages needed.'
suggested_fix: Scope the lookup to the form: const field = name => document.getElementById('toolForm').elements[name] (or use the element ids). Add a real-DOM browser regression that types a description, saves and checks the API/re-opened editor; the fake-DOM unit tests cannot catch this because they lack the <meta> tag.

title: Run / Test (and MCP tools/call) blocks the whole server: synchronous subprocess.run inside async handlers
failure_scenario: api_run_tool and mcp_endpoint are 'async def' but call run_tool() -> subprocess.run() (and dependency installs) synchronously on the event loop. While one Run / Test is in progress (up to timeout+15 s, plus up to 120 s install and 125 s lock wait), every other request queues: other dashboard tabs show 'Loading tools…'/'Checking workspace…', the Connect page spinner never resolves, and MCP clients' tools/list and calls hang or time out. A single slow tool test makes the AI client fail.
evidence: Verified: started POST /api/tools/sleeper/run (time.sleep(20)), then GET /api/config took 18.48 s, finishing just after the run (20.02 s). Code: main.py:169 async def api_run_tool -> :182 run_tool(); main.py:196/241 async mcp_endpoint -> handler.call_tool -> mcp_server.py:141 run_tool().
suggested_fix: Declare these endpoints with plain 'def' (FastAPI runs them in the threadpool) or wrap the call: result = await run_in_threadpool(run_tool, tool, arguments). Consider an execution semaphore so concurrent runs cannot exhaust the threadpool. Then remove the 'may block other requests' caveat only once verified.

title: Library list is never re-fetched on navigation, so the advertised 412 recovery loops forever and MCP-created/deleted tools are invisible
failure_scenario: The tools array is loaded only at startup, after this tab's own writes, on the 'online' event, or via Retry after an error. The 412 message tells the user to 'Reload from the library', but going to Tools and reopening the tool uses the same stale in-memory row (old code, old revision), so Run, Save, Toggle and Delete all return 412 again until a full page reload. On the Tools page the toggle 412 toast also says 'draft retained', which is meaningless there. Tools created by an LLM through omniforge_create_tool never appear (counts stay wrong; deep link says 'This tool is unavailable'), and a tool deleted elsewhere stays listed and opens a ghost editor whose Run returns 'HTTP 404: Tool not found'.
evidence: Verified (s3_state.cjs, s11_misc.cjs): node_echo changed by another client -> Run 412; Tools -> reopen -> list still 'Echo args' (server 'Edited elsewhere v2'); Run 412 again; Save 412; toggle 412 twice ('...draft retained...'). MCP-created mcp_made: after Overview/Help/Tools navigation libraryCount '6 of 6', not listed; #tools/edit/mcp_made -> 'This tool is unavailable'. victim deleted by API: Run -> 'HTTP 404: Tool not found', row still listed.
suggested_fix: Call loadTools() when entering #tools / #overview and before opening #tools/edit/NAME (cheap GET), and on visibilitychange/focus. After a 412/404 trigger loadTools() and offer an explicit 'Reload this tool from server' action that re-fills the editor (after a copy/confirm). Use a page-appropriate 412 message for toggles.

title: Cross-site requests can toggle and execute tools: body-less POST /toggle and /run are CSRF-able 'simple' requests
failure_scenario: The UI tells users the dashboard is safe on a 'trusted network', but any web page the user visits from that network can fire fetch(..., {method:'POST', mode:'no-cors'}) at http://<omniforge>/api/tools/<name>/toggle or /run. Neither needs a body, a JSON content type or a header, so no CORS preflight occurs: the attacker silently disables/enables tools for AI discovery and executes any saved tool (which shares the app container's environment and credentials). Tool names are easy to guess (example_python_requests etc.). DELETE/PUT are protected only incidentally, by preflight. Chrome's newer Local Network Access prompt mitigates this for public sites, but not for Firefox/Safari, nor for any page on the same LAN/loopback.
evidence: Verified: a page served from a different origin (http://localhost:18399) ran no-cors POSTs; exit_124 flipped is_active true -> false (state restored afterwards), and server.log shows 'POST /api/tools/exit_124/run HTTP/1.1 200 OK' from that page. DELETE was blocked (OPTIONS 405).
suggested_fix: Require a non-simple signal on every mutating/executing endpoint: e.g. reject requests without 'Content-Type: application/json' or a custom header (X-OmniForge: 1) that the dashboard always sends, and/or check Origin/Sec-Fetch-Site == same-origin. Validate the Host header against an allowlist to stop DNS rebinding. Update the 'trusted network' copy to mention that browsers on that network are part of the trust boundary until auth exists.

title: After a deploy, new dashboard HTML is rendered with the old cached CSS/fonts until the user finds and clicks 'Update available'
failure_scenario: HTML is network-only but product.css/fonts are served cache-first from the old worker's cache, and the new worker waits (no skipWaiting) while any tab is open. After every release that changes CSS, users get new markup + old styles on every reload, indefinitely, unless they click the small 'Update available' button or close every tab. Any release that forgets to bump CACHE never updates styles at all, because nothing ties the cache name to asset content.
evidence: Verified on a scratch COPY of the app (fe-copy.sh, port 18303): released new markup <span class="release-marker">, a CSS rule color: rgb(1,2,3) and bumped CACHE to v3. After reload: new markup present, computed colour rgb(24,44,42) (old CSS), caches [v2, v3], waiting worker, Update button shown; a second reload was still stale. Only after clicking Update did the colour become rgb(1, 2, 3).
suggested_fix: Version asset URLs (e.g. /assets/product.css?v=<hash> or hashed filenames) emitted by the HTML so new HTML always requests new assets, and let the worker cache by full URL; or serve allowlisted assets network-first with cache fallback. Add a test that fails when any ASSETS file hash changes without a CACHE change.

title: Tab/Shift+Tab indentation uses setRangeText, which wipes the editor's undo history
failure_scenario: A user types code, presses Tab to indent, then presses Ctrl+Z to undo a mistake: nothing happens, and nothing typed before the Tab can be undone any more. On a script editor, losing undo after the most common editing key is a real work-loss risk.
evidence: Verified in Chromium (s5/s7): typed 'abc', Home, Tab -> '  abc'; Ctrl+Z twice -> still '  abc'. Control without Tab: typing then Ctrl+Z undoes normally.
suggested_fix: Insert indentation with document.execCommand('insertText', false, text) after setting the selection (still the only cross-browser way to keep the native undo stack), falling back to setRangeText only when execCommand returns false; for block indent replace the selected line range via insertText.

title: Test inputs and displayed output are round-tripped through JS numbers: large IDs, decimals and duplicate keys are silently changed
failure_scenario: runSaved() JSON.parses Test inputs and re-stringifies them, and the output panel JSON.parses stdout and pretty-prints it. A tool taking a 64-bit ID (Discord/Twitter snowflakes, database keys > 2^53) is tested with order_id 9007199254740993 but actually receives 9007199254740992 - it may act on a different record. The output panel likewise shows numbers and structures that differ from what MCP clients receive (1.0 shown as 1, duplicate keys collapsed), misleading debugging.
evidence: Verified: echo_any with inputs {"order_id": 9007199254740993, "amount": 10.10, "flag": 1.0} -> displayed {"order_id": 9007199254740992, "amount": 10.1, "flag": 1}. big_numbers raw stdout {"id": 9007199254740993, "ratio": 1.0, "dup": 1, "dup": 2} displayed as {"id": 9007199254740992, "ratio": 1, "dup": 2}. Code: line 392 JSON.parse(testInputs), line 404 JSON.stringify, line 408 output reformat.
suggested_fix: Validate the inputs with JSON.parse but send the raw text: body: '{"arguments":' + textarea.value + '}' (still Content-Type JSON). Show stdout verbatim (optionally offer a 'pretty' toggle that warns when JSON.stringify(JSON.parse(x)) loses information, e.g. compare against a lossless check for integers > Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER).

title: Connect 'HTTP request template' omits Content-Type: application/json; copying its headers into curl returns 422
failure_scenario: The template's headers contain only Authorization. A user reproducing it with curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer ...' -d '{...}' gets a FastAPI 422 'Input should be a valid dictionary' (curl -d defaults to application/x-www-form-urlencoded), with no hint why. The snippet is also a custom {endpoint, method, headers, body} shape rather than a config any MCP client accepts, so users must translate it by hand.
evidence: Verified: POST /mcp with only the template's Authorization header and curl -d -> {"detail":[{"type":"dict_type",..."Input should be a valid dictionary"}]}; adding -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -> tools/list result.
suggested_fix: Always include 'Content-Type': 'application/json' (and 'Accept': 'application/json') in the template, and add a ready-to-paste curl command plus, where compatible, a client config example (e.g. mcpServers {url, headers}) using the same placeholder.

title: Tool-name pattern attribute is an invalid v-flag regex: browser logs an error and client-side name validation is disabled
failure_scenario: Chrome compiles HTML pattern attributes with the RegExp 'v' flag, where an unescaped '-' at the end of a character class is a syntax error. The pattern is ignored (console error on every editor visit), so 'bad name!' passes reportValidity(). Saving then fails only with a toast 'HTTP 422: Value error, Invalid tool name...'; #nameError stays hidden and aria-invalid is not set, so screen-reader and keyboard users get no field-level error.
evidence: Verified: console 'Pattern attribute value [a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9_-]{0,62} is not a valid regular expression ... /v: Invalid character in character class' on every editor load; '1 bad name!' -> validity.patternMismatch false, checkValidity() true. Saving 'bad name!' -> toast only, nameError hidden, aria-invalid null.
suggested_fix: Escape the hyphen: pattern="[a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9_\-]{0,62}" (valid with and without v). Also map HTTP 422 name errors to #nameError/aria-invalid like the 409 path.

title: 'Update available' stays visible and does nothing in other tabs after the update is accepted elsewhere
failure_scenario: Every open tab receives updatefound and shows 'Update available'. When the user accepts in tab A, tab B keeps its button; clicking it posts SKIP_WAITING to the already-active worker, no controllerchange fires, nothing reloads and the button never disappears.
evidence: Verified on the scratch copy (s10_update.cjs): tab B showed the button before accept; after tab A accepted, tab B button still visible; clicking it left the same document and the button visible after 2 s.
suggested_fix: Listen for controllerchange in every tab (hide the button and show 'Updated in another tab - reload when ready'), and in the click handler check waitingWorker.state; if it is already 'activated', just offer a guarded reload.

title: A script that exits with code 124 is reported in the studio as a timeout
failure_scenario: timed_out is derived from exit_code == 124 instead of the TimeoutExpired path, so a script that deliberately exits 124 (or wraps GNU timeout) shows 'Failed · exit 124 · 21 ms · timeout'. The real timeout message also says 'exceeded 30000ms' although the limit applied is timeout + 15 s.
evidence: Verified: exit_124 tool (prints 'done', sys.exit(124)) -> runSummary 'Failed · exit 124 · 21 ms · timeout'. Code: runner.py:95 message, :103 timed_out=(exit_code == 124).
suggested_fix: Track a separate timed_out boolean set in the except subprocess.TimeoutExpired branch, and report the effective limit (MAX_TIMEOUT_MS + 15000) in the message.

title: Validation feedback in the studio is generic or hidden: schema errors don't say which field, package errors leave the Packages section collapsed
failure_scenario: A tool with required inputs is run with the default {} or a wrong type: the output only says 'HTTP 422: Arguments do not match inputSchema', with no property/path, while the saved schema is inside a collapsed 'Packages & advanced settings' disclosure. An invalid package line saves with a toast only; the requirements textarea stays hidden in the collapsed <details> and is not marked invalid.
evidence: Verified: greet_schema with {} and with {"name":"Ada","times":"three"} -> 'HTTP 422: Arguments do not match inputSchema'; #advancedSettings open=false. Packages 'requests>=2' -> toast 'HTTP 422: Value error, Invalid requirement...', details still closed.
suggested_fix: Return a value-free location, e.g. 'Missing required property "name"' or '/times: expected integer' (validator, path and schema keyword, never the submitted value). In the UI, open #advancedSettings and set aria-invalid on #toolRequirements for requirement errors, and show the schema's required fields next to Test inputs.

title: Offline fallback says 'Your workspace is online.' and ignores dark mode
failure_scenario: A user whose connection dropped opens OmniForge and sees the headline 'Your workspace is online.' under 'Connection needed' - it reads as a contradiction. The page has no theme script and the CSS has no prefers-color-scheme rules, so dark-mode users get a bright light page.
evidence: Verified offline navigation via the service worker: title 'Reconnect · OmniForge', h1 'Your workspace is online.', body background rgb(247, 248, 245) with prefers-color-scheme: dark.
suggested_fix: Reword, e.g. 'We can't reach your workspace'. Add @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) token overrides in product.css (applies to both pages when no explicit data-theme is set) or a tiny inline theme script reading omniforge-theme.

title: Connection indicator stays 'online' teal when offline or the server is unavailable; Ctrl+S offline gives no feedback
failure_scenario: The status dot before 'Offline' / 'Server unavailable' is always var(--accent), the same colour as 'Workspace online', so the only visual cue is text. Pressing Ctrl+S while offline silently does nothing (save() returns early without notify), leaving users unsure whether their work was saved.
evidence: Verified offline in-tab: state 'Offline', ::before background rgb(155, 226, 200) == --accent; Ctrl+S with unsaved edits -> no status toast, saveState still 'Unsaved changes'.
suggested_fix: Add a data-state on #connectionState and colour the dot with --warn/--danger for offline/unavailable. In save()/runSaved() call notify('You're offline - changes are kept in this tab', true) instead of returning silently.

title: Enable/disable switch's accessible name is the action, contradicting its state
failure_scenario: An enabled tool's switch is named 'Disable <name>' with aria-checked=true, so screen readers announce 'Disable many_lines, switch, on' - users cannot tell whether 'on' means enabled or disabled. The name also changes on every toggle.
evidence: Verified accessibility tree: switch "Disable many_lines" [checked]: Enabled.
suggested_fix: Use a stable name describing the setting, e.g. aria-label='Enabled for AI: <name>' (or aria-labelledby the tool name plus a visually hidden 'enabled for AI'), and let aria-checked carry the state.

title: 'Escape, then Shift+Tab' does not leave the code editor and unindents the current line instead
failure_scenario: The leaveEditor flag is cleared by any non-Tab keydown, and pressing Shift fires a keydown for 'Shift' first. A keyboard user who presses Escape then Shift+Tab to go back to the Name field stays trapped in the editor and silently modifies their code.
evidence: Verified: code '    line one', Escape, Shift+Tab -> focus still #toolCode, code became '  line one'. Escape then Tab correctly moves to the Packages summary.
suggested_fix: Ignore pure modifier keys when resetting the flag (if (['Shift','Control','Alt','Meta'].includes(e.key)) return;), and mention Shift+Tab in the hint.

title: Scrollable output and request-template <pre> regions are not focusable (axe 'scrollable-region-focusable', serious)
failure_scenario: Long Test output (max-height 360px) and, at 320px width, the Connect request template become scroll containers without tabindex. In Safari/iOS (the documented Add-to-Home-Screen path), keyboard and switch users cannot scroll them to read the rest of the output; Chromium/Firefox only work thanks to their focusable-scroller heuristics.
evidence: Verified with axe 4.11: many_lines output (scrollHeight 2699 > 358) -> scrollable-region-focusable on '#out pre.ok'; Connect at 320x640 in both themes -> same rule on #requestTemplate. (#savedInputSchema already has tabindex=0.)
suggested_fix: Give #out pre and #requestTemplate tabindex="0" plus an accessible name (aria-label='Test output' / 'HTTP request template'), as already done for #savedInputSchema. Add 320px to the browser axe matrix.

title: viewport-fit=cover without left/right safe-area padding: rail and topbar sit under the notch in phone landscape
failure_scenario: Phones in landscape are wider than 640px, so they get the desktop rail layout (padding-left 12px). With viewport-fit=cover, on a notched iPhone in landscape (safe-area-inset-left ~47px) the logo and nav icons are drawn under the sensor housing / rounded corner. Only safe-area-inset-bottom is handled.
evidence: Measured at 844x390 and 667x375: .rail padding-left 12px; product.css contains env(safe-area-inset-bottom) only (lines 29, 978); dashboard.html line 5 sets viewport-fit=cover. Chromium cannot emulate insets, so the overlap itself was not rendered.
suggested_fix: Add padding-left: max(12px, env(safe-area-inset-left)) to .rail, and padding-right: max(24px, env(safe-area-inset-right)) to .topbar/.page in the <=1023px and landscape ranges.

title: Cancelling a dirty Back navigation overwrites the previous history entry
failure_scenario: When the user presses Back with unsaved edits and cancels, history.replaceState rewrites the entry they were going back to (#tools) with the editor URL. The next accepted Back skips Tools and lands on an older entry, e.g. a previously opened tool's editor (which may no longer exist).
evidence: Verified (s11_misc.cjs): history ... #tools/edit/victim, #tools, #tools/edit/many_lines (dirty). Back -> Cancel -> hash #tools/edit/many_lines; Back again -> landed on #tools/edit/victim instead of #tools.
suggested_fix: On cancel, restore with history.go(1) (forward) or pushState the editor route instead of replaceState, so the #tools entry is preserved.

title: Every keystroke rebuilds the whole line-number gutter: typing lags on large scripts
failure_scenario: updateGutter() splits the full code and rebuilds a string of all line numbers on each input event. Pasting generated code or embedded data (20k-50k lines) makes each keystroke take ~90-225 ms, making the editor feel frozen.
evidence: Measured real typing in Chromium: 5k lines 25 ms/keystroke, 20k lines 89 ms, 50k lines 225 ms; gutter rebuild alone 13/53/132 ms; fingerprinting cost negligible (<=2 ms).
suggested_fix: Track the line count and only append/trim gutter lines when it changes (or update in requestAnimationFrame), so normal typing costs O(1).

title: At 320px the editor action buttons squeeze 'Run / Test' onto three lines
failure_scenario: On the smallest supported phones the three footer buttons share one row with flex:1, so the primary test action renders as 'Run' / '/' / 'Test' stacked in a tall button, which looks broken.
evidence: Screenshot shots/editor-320x640.png: Delete | Run / / Test | Save tool. (375px renders correctly.)
suggested_fix: Use white-space: nowrap on footer buttons and let .actions wrap (flex-wrap: wrap with flex: 1 1 auto), or stack the actions full-width below 360px.
